quarterly_data.signal: CALL - FY2026 AND Q4 P&L DETAIL: CEO Satya Nadella said Azure surpassed $100 billion in fiscal 2026, up 41%. CFO Amy Hood: fiscal-year operating income grew faster than revenue, increasing 21% to more than $155 billion. Q4: revenue up 17% in constant currency; gross margin dollars up 15%; earnings per share $4.74, up 23% when adjusted for the impact of the OpenAI investment; discrete items versus the April guidance added $0.27 of EPS (the Anthropic gain and lower-than-expected voluntary retirement program expense, partially offset by severance expense and Xbox impairment charges). Company gross margin was 67%, down year over year on the sales mix shift to Azure and continued AI infrastructure investment and growing product usage, partially offset by efficiency gains in Azure and M365 commercial cloud; operating expenses rose 10% on R&D compute capacity, talent and data; operating margin increased slightly to 45%; total headcount declined 2%. Microsoft Cloud gross margin was 'better than expected at 65%' and down year over year.

quarterly_data.signal: CALL - M365 COPILOT ADOPTION AND THE SEAT-PLUS-CONSUMPTION MODEL (CEO Satya Nadella): Copilot user satisfaction scores doubled over the last three quarters to an all-time high, latency was cut 25% this quarter, conversations per user nearly doubled year over year, and average weekly engagement is on par with Outlook and Teams; the time from deployment to high usage (about 80% monthly active usage) fell from months to days; enterprise customers deploying Copilot to the majority of their information workers grew nearly 75% quarter over quarter. Deployments: KPMG is expanding across its more than 276,000 professionals, HSBC committed to 200,000 seats, and AstraZeneca, Boeing, Infosys, Coke Inc., Procter & Gamble, Stellantis, Tata Consultancy Services, University of Pittsburgh Medical Center, Wells Fargo and Wipro each purchased 60,000 or more. For the E7 suite (Copilot, E5, Entra and Agent 365), hundreds of enterprise customers bought millions of seats within two months of launch. Microsoft is moving from per seat to per seat plus consumption: usage-based billing added to Copilot Cowork already has thousands of paying customers; Dynamics 365 exposes over 650,000 MCP actions to agents, and usage-based credit consumption in customer service rose 4x quarter over quarter. Chat, Cowork, Autopilot and Code are being brought together into one 'super app' spanning consumer and commercial. CFO Amy Hood: E7 was in market only part of the quarter and Microsoft was 'quite encouraged by the value customers saw in that SKU'.
quarterly_data.figure: Copilot latency cut 25%; majority-of-workforce Copilot deployments up nearly 75% QoQ; HSBC 200,000 seats; customer-service credit consumption 4x QoQ

quarterly_data.signal: CALL Q&A - DEMAND CYCLE RISK AND ROI: CFO Amy Hood said demand currently exceeds available supply 'in a sort of relatively extreme moment', and process improvements over the past 90 days shortened the lead time to get CPUs and GPUs plugged in, a dynamic she expects in Q1 too. On the risk that demand changes she added that land and data center builds are 'a smaller percentage of the overall cost structure', that Microsoft can 'late bind some of the more expensive components', and that a diverse book of business by geography, segment and industry plus its own first-party apps can use the capacity being built. CEO Satya Nadella: 'there will be ups and downs of what is the cycle here, but the secular shift is clear.' On ROI, Hood said 'I don't know that, quite frankly, my math has changed' over the past year; her greater confidence in the return on invested capital comes from TAM expansion and margin levers - silicon price-performance including first-party investments, model diversification ('also is a margin improvement opportunity'), token efficiency and running at hyperscale.

CALL - RISING COMPONENT PRICES (CFO Amy Hood): Windows OEM results were ahead of expectations 'as OEM and channel partners continued to build inventory given increasing component prices'. FY2027: Windows OEM and devices growth will be impacted by lower PC market demand as higher component costs increase device pricing, a prior year that benefited from Windows 10 end of support, and elevated inventory levels, so revenue is expected to decline in the high teens. FQ1 FY2027: Windows OEM and devices revenue should decline in the low 20s amid 'complex PC market dynamics impacted by component prices and inventory levels', with a wider than normal range of outcomes. In Q&A she said component price increases are 'impacting everybody equivalently'; Microsoft is responding with efficiency work, a lot of the capacity it is adding is being sold in newer contracts whose pricing reflects the higher costs, and the cloud still gives customers a better ROI than buying servers on-premises, where the price increases are harder on them.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2027 Windows OEM and devices revenue to decline in the high teens; FQ1 FY2027 decline in the low 20s
